Bullet 1 says it is permitted with a possibly-null result, and §14.2 ("zero/null value of T") and bullet 4's own ground ("the null value `default(T)` would produce") presuppose that at a reference substitution it yields null. An interface method is never `async` (the modifier is invisible in signatures, §28.12), so a call `r.Go<Pair>(…)` meets no §30.1 rule, and the implementing `async method Go<T>(x: T)`'s frame captures x. §30.1 makes the parameter check an instantiation-site re-check 'for a generic async method'; §14.2's dispatched rule moves to the body only 'an interior use read at the substitution' and 'an instantiation the body forms', and calls the exclusion 'an instantiation-site rule' of another kind. Reading A: the re-check is a requirement decided at the body (error unless the declaring method's constraints establish non-holds-borrows; borrow-flow R8×C9's note assumes this). Reading B: it is an instantiation-site rule, which dispatch reaches at no site, so the Pair enters the frame unbounded (K4.1 backstops the Item read). Same root cause as R4×C13 (G3). Codegen-reference defects found while hunting: G8.

OPEN (verdict-only): §14.6 attributes an override's edges to the overridden member's node and checks cross-module cycles 'over the compilation closure'. Two implementations in sibling modules M2 and M3, each depending only on M1, contribute the two halves of an expanding SCC between M1's interface methods; neither M2's nor M3's closure holds the cycle. Reading A: the root compilation whose closure first holds both (App, importing M2 and M3) is rejected, the diagnostic at a declaration in another module. Reading B: each declaration is checked only in its own module's compilation, so the program is admitted with an unbounded instantiation closure. Under both readings, if App reaches M2 and M3 only through a module whose interface does not reference them, no compilation closure holds the cycle.

Reading B: the list is the definition; a type reached only through its statics is never instantiated at a site, so no §3.6 rule 2 requirement of it is read.
